content:
If you've been testing Apple Watch beta apps all summer, you may have noticed that some existing apps fail to launch on watchOS 27. Apple has confirmed the issue and is now automatically pushing updates out on behalf of developers.

The relevant updates are rolling out via the App Store, with the update notes reading: "This app was updated by Apple to prepare for compatibility with watchOS 27. No new features."

Apple informed developers earlier this week that the entire update process will be completed by August 31.

watchOS 27, along with iOS 27 and other new operating systems, is expected to be officially released to the public around mid-September, so these necessary updates should be completed before the official launch.

Apple explained that because some watchOS apps have issues on the arm64 architecture, this measure is necessary. Reports indicate that the company is automatically reprocessing and repackaging affected apps to fix binary compatibility issues, allowing existing apps to continue functioning normally without developers needing to take additional action.
